scope: Static CSDL 4.01 XML/JSON authoring and tolerant consumption; source paragraphs are in conformance-requirements.json. Prefix matching uses the longest section prefix.

status_meaning.covered: Direct implementation and regression evidence for this paragraph; not a blanket certification of its enclosing section.
status_meaning.partial: Implementation and tests exist, but known behavior or direct positive/negative evidence remains incomplete.
status_meaning.unsupported: A known static obligation is not implemented completely.
status_meaning.advisory: SHOULD guidance deliberately does not reject otherwise valid documents.
status_meaning.outside-static-scope: Transport, runtime data, execution, or specification metarule; no static validator assertion is appropriate.

groups.note: RFC requirement-word interpretation; not an executable CSDL constraint.
HTTP content negotiation belongs to the hosting service. JSON media-type output options are implemented separately from HTTP negotiation.
Prose takes precedence over schemas; the audit includes semantic checks beyond document shape.
Member, parameter, and expression order retained. The syntactic model groups structural/navigation members and container children by kind, so it cannot reproduce all interleaving.
Names and scope identity checked. Case-only differences remain advisory; programmatic models need the source checks supplied by guarded serialization.
Term identity plus qualifier plus resolved target identify duplicate applications.

Document grammar, service intent, includes, loader cache, cycles and alias scope implemented. Reference and Include annotations are retained and resolved. DocumentLoader::inspect_reference exposes Core.SchemaVersion before retrieval, including cache hits; strict JSON alias-only spelling is enforced.
Schema, alias and annotation group validation implemented. Strict JSON parsing enforces alias-only references; tolerant resolution accepts both spellings.
Static identity/inheritance rules covered by both-format tests; data-instance obligations are runtime responsibilities.
Key paths, types, aliases and related-entity key coverage checked. Actual key uniqueness and language-independent URLs are outside the static model.

Names, types, facets, defaults and version differences checked. Imported primitive ABNF cases execute in XML and JSON; unrepresentable unknown collection-nullability conversion is rejected. Exhaustive facet evidence remains partial.
Partners, constraints, containment, cardinality and delete declarations are checked; row values, relationship integrity and executing delete actions are outside static validation.
Complex inheritance and declaration rules implemented; case-only names advisory, dynamic instance properties outside scope.
Enum declarations and implicit XML values checked. JSON annotation numeric enum values and all flag combinations need further expression tests.
Underlying types and inherited facets checked; expand direct XML/JSON cases for every abstract type use.

Overloads, binding and return types checked. Authored-versus-defaulted nullability is preserved for JSON collection signatures. Cross-version parameter order and function side effects require a service/history context.
Container identity, inheritance and unique child names checked. Service-data and queryability recommendations belong to the host.

Resolved binding graph semantics checked. JSON same-container target spelling is validated and normalized during options output; recursive-path variants need more clause evidence. Missing bindings remain advisory.
Import overload identity, unbound requirement, target entity-set identity and return compatibility checked; not every clause yet has an independent paired-format case.
See action imports; function imports retain unbound overload candidates.

Semantic diagnostics remain nonfatal for tolerant consumers. Profile parsing recovers invalid/unavailable annotation expressions with optional ParseReport diagnostics. Legacy APIs preserve their error behavior.
Term/default/base-term/applicability checks implemented; per-member record completion from base-term applications is implemented.
Targets and term casts use resolved graph nodes. Document scope checks include structural and annotation paths; exhaustive clause evidence remains partial.

Common lexical forms/ranges/facets tested. The official ABNF corpus is imported and classified; 66 primitive/identifier cases execute with explicit representation adaptation. Arbitrary decimal text, numeric enums and source-format literal typing are implemented; complete clause evidence remains partial.
Operators, metadata, casts and records implemented with recursive checks. See more specific path/function/record limitations.

Typed key/index selectors, counts, empty paths, collection multiplicity, media terms, navigation annotation suffixes, and target-relative contexts are implemented. Literal domains and exhaustive clause-level evidence remain partial.

Declared functions and common canonical functions checked. Full canonical overload catalog, numeric promotion, geography functions, custom client-function registries and URI-template map typing remain incomplete.
Arity, Boolean condition, branch compatibility and collection-only omitted else checked; execution is outside scope.
Labels bind by canonical schema name, cycles and duplicates are diagnostic. Add all cross-document visibility and nested-expression annotation cases.
See labeled elements; unresolved names are explicit diagnostics.
Record members, abstract types, duplicates and required values checked. Base-term member inheritance and typed open records require additional checks.
URL operand is checked as String. Returned resource representation needs caller-supplied type/evaluation context; no HTTP fetch occurs.
Version guards and consumption/authoring profiles are explicit. The remaining partial/unsupported rows preclude a full service or client conformance claim.

overrides.note: Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover 4.0/4.01 singleton and scalar navigation targets with/without keys, including ordinary and containment navigation. Keyless targets validate only in 4.01; declared keys validate in both versions.

Independent XML/JSON cases prove property name uniqueness including navigation collisions, required XML names/types, rejected malformed JSON types, and resolved Edm.String for omitted JSON types on entity and complex owners.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover entity, complex, enum and type-definition identifiers, including Unicode and underscore positives and empty/qualified/numeric-leading/space negatives. Pairwise schema collisions cover all type kinds, terms, functions, actions and containers; distinct and case-only names validate.

Independent XML/JSON cases prove member-name uniqueness and identifier syntax, including Unicode/underscore names, case-only distinctions, duplicates, empty names and qualified-name rejection. Advisory case-collision policy remains non-rejecting.
Independent XML cases reject missing Name with and without Value, preserve omitted/explicit values and verify resolved ordinal/explicit values with semantic validation.

Independent XML/JSON cases reject missing names/kinds and malformed kind values, retain omitted and explicit optional base/Boolean attributes, structural and navigation properties and annotations, and validate accepted declarations.

Independent XML/JSON source cases prove numeric/variable SRID values and malformed-value rejection. Geometry/geography default-value matrices prove omitted defaults of 0/4326, explicit numeric overrides, variable SRIDs and mismatch rejection.
Independent XML/JSON property fixtures accept lowercase, uppercase and mixed-case variable/floating scales in both profiles, preserve resolved facets and emit lowercase in both strict output formats.

Independent XML matrix covers string/binary properties, 4.0/4.01, strict/tolerant profiles and omitted/numeric/max values. Consumers preserve max and absent limits through resolution; strict 4.01 parsing/output reject max before output bytes, and permitted forms round-trip.

Independent XML matrix covers 4.0/4.01, scalar/collection and omitted/false/true Nullable in strict/tolerant profiles. Strict 4.01 authors must specify collection Nullable; tolerant consumers retain omitted nullability as unknown in syntactic and resolved models without inventing a default.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures on entity and complex owners prove scalar/collection primitive, complex, enum and type-definition resolution, reject entity and missing local/foreign types, and assert resolved multiplicity.
Independent JSON fixtures prove omitted/false/true collection controls and retained item type, reject XML collection type spelling and non-Boolean controls, and validate accepted declarations.

Independent XML/JSON cases prove required source names/kinds, reject missing or malformed kinds, retain omitted and explicit optional base/Boolean attributes, and resolve and validate valid declarations.

Independent XML cases reject each missing required attribute and prove retention and semantic acceptance of optional Nullable, MaxLength, Unicode, Precision, Scale, SRID and DefaultValue attributes on applicable types.
Independent XML source cases reject missing Name with and without Alias, retain direct and aliased paths, and resolve and validate both valid declaration forms.

Independent authored XML proves schema order, enum member order/implicit ordinal values, operation parameter positions and collection item order/duplicates through parsing, resolution and XML/JSON round trips. Arbitrary interleaving of different child kinds remains to be reviewed because the syntactic model uses separate child vectors in several locations.

JSON parser fixtures assert retained expression variants for scalar constants, collections, records, paths and every dynamic operator family. Unknown/malformed/multiple discriminators fail strict parsing; tolerant recovery drops the whole annotation, including nested failures, while retaining neighboring declarations. Operand type compatibility is separately validated by semantic suites.

JSON fixtures prove item-type resolution and omitted/false/true Collection controls, rejecting XML collection type syntax and nonboolean controls. Explicit true/false/null values survive term defaults, and a default does not invent an absent annotation.

Independent XML/JSON tests cover label shape/scope, type and multiplicity propagation across annotation contexts, and cycle termination. Reviewed obligations separate static checks from runtime value evaluation; mixed paragraphs remain partial.

Independent XML/JSON tests bind qualified entity/complex casts, reject unqualified cast spellings, missing types and indirectly loaded namespaces, and preserve same-family runtime cast possibilities. Static scope and runtime null evaluation are decomposed into reviewed obligations.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures resolve child members and traverse navigation targets across three successive references. Missing members at every level fail; indirectly loaded namespaces remain unavailable to explicit casts and absolute roots in the original document.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover qualified term names, qualifiers including Unicode and malformed forms, missing terms and all four implicit media terms on media entities/stream properties versus nonmedia targets. Static resolution and runtime missing-application null behavior are decomposed in reviewed obligations.

Independent XML/JSON instance paths enforce the unselected-collection limit and preserve multiplicity after key/index selection. Runtime per-instance evaluation is separately scoped in reviewed atomic obligations.

Independent XML/JSON scalar/collection endpoint matrices cover primitive, complex, enum, type-definition and entity types, plus applied terms. PropertyPath and NavigationPropertyPath enforce their type families; AnnotationPath requires an annotation endpoint. Wrong endpoints and missing members produce explicit InvalidExpressionPath diagnostics.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures across all five path kinds cover empty and multisegment relative paths, qualified absolute roots and root-relative traversal. Unqualified or absent absolute roots, doubled separators and trailing empty segments are rejected. Absolute roots are checked before default-namespace qualification.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover all five path kinds on embedded/external entity and complex type annotations. Empty paths retain the annotated type; structural/navigation traversal, type casts and term casts resolve; missing members/types/terms fail. Endpoint validation is checked separately from segment resolution.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover all five path-expression kinds on embedded/external container, set and singleton annotations: empty-path target identity, every container child kind, selectors, properties, navigation and casts. All kinds reject container term casts before a child segment. Endpoint-specific validation and value-only selectors are checked independently from segment resolution.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover embedded/external annotations on actions, functions, their imports, parameters and returns. Parameter and $ReturnType prefixes succeed; missing/unprefixed/empty paths fail. Annotation-count assertions prevent silent omission, and parser-only tests preserve operation-level JSON annotations in both profiles.

Independent XML/JSON structural/navigation-property fixtures on complex/entity owners prove enclosing versus outermost context, empty-path type identity, nested structural/navigation traversal and wrong-context/missing-property rejection. Type and term casts cover valid names and missing names; incompatible same-family casts remain statically valid because runtime evaluation can produce null.

Independent XML/JSON conditional fixtures check both branches against expected primitive/structured types, numeric promotion, nullability and collection shape, with true/false conditions. XML zero-through-four operand cases and inline-attribute rejection prove element-only notation and permitted arity. Runtime branch evaluation is separately scoped.

Independent XML/JSON target paths cover qualified roots, derived-type segments, applied terms and operation signatures with scalar/collection parameter types. Included aliases and Edm types resolve; missing or loaded-but-not-included namespaces do not. Signature visibility checks every explicitly named parameter type.

Independent XML/JSON references exercise included and aliased annotation terms/targets, missing names and hidden namespaces loaded as dependencies but excluded from the root scope. Applicability restrictions have independent strict/tolerant evidence.

Strict XML requires Term and permits optional Qualifier. Parent/child qualifier combinations prove inheritance and reject child redeclaration when the group has a qualifier, including equal values, before normalization loses authored placement.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover unrestricted terms, single/multiple applicability values, unknown future values and mixed known/unknown lists. Both parser profiles retain the documents; strict validation diagnoses disallowed targets while tolerant validation remains valid and reports NotApplicable.

Independent XML/JSON three-term chains require every ancestor on the same target with the same qualifier. The matrix covers absent ancestors, wrong qualifiers, different targets, qualified and unqualified applications, and exact leaf MissingBaseTerm diagnostics.

Independent XML/JSON term defaults cover Boolean, integer boundaries, floating, decimal, binary, GUID and temporal lexical values; parsed string assertions prove XML attribute escaping and whitespace preservation. Spatial cases cover all geography/geometry shapes, shape mismatch, SRID and malformed coordinates; facet cases cover direct and type-definition length, Unicode, decimal and temporal constraints.

Independent XML/JSON declarations cover identifier syntax and schema name collisions, scalar/collection built-in and user-defined type scope, required XML Name/Type and JSON Term kind, plus optional base-term and applicability fields.

Independent XML/JSON cases cover minimum arity, scalar primitive/enum/type-definition operands, collection/structured rejection and string result typing. Runtime literal conversion and concatenation are separately scoped in conformance-obligations.json.
Independent XML source cases accept empty Null elements and reject Null attribute notation and expression children. Strict parsing no longer silently ignores a Null attribute.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures accept supplied qualified client functions and reject unqualified names, reserved odata custom names and attempts to replace builtin signatures.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures require function references and exercise operand expressions, builtin signatures and concat arity. Runtime function execution remains outside static validation.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover required structural/navigation members, nullable/defaulted/collection omissions and direct/transitive base-term completion. The three-level matrix checks leaf diagnostics for every combination of missing required values.
Independent XML/JSON entity and complex records cover inferred context types, explicit base/derived types, and rejection of primitive, unrelated and unresolved types.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover valid record property values; XML cases explicitly require Property and one expression, accepting attribute and element notation.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures reject invalid/empty label names and duplicates within one expression or across annotations in a schema, while accepting distinct names and identical names in separate schemas.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover required names and valid label values; XML fixtures accept attribute/element expression notation and reject missing or excess child expressions.
Independent XML label-reference bodies and JSON reference values cover qualified in-scope names, missing labels/namespaces and invalid unqualified references.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover empty/primitive collections, numeric promotion, incompatible members, nested collections, nonnullable null items and scalar/collection mismatches. Explicit complex records now cover base/derived compatibility and unrelated/unresolved type rejection. Dynamic arithmetic/comparison/cast/type-test/builtin/conditional/label items and enum/type-definition members/facets now have independent evidence. Entity records now cover concrete base/derived compatibility with keys, and path/caller-supplied function/URL items cover type and scalar multiplicity. Static branches are decomposed into covered obligations; runtime collection evaluation keeps the mixed paragraph partial.

XML fixtures require Type and exactly one child expression. Independently authored XML/JSON fixtures accept one typed operand and reject unresolved target types. JSON null remains an expression rather than an absent XML child.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover zero through three operands for Neg and Add/Sub/Mul/Div/DivBy/Mod, accepting only unary/binary arity as appropriate and rejecting Boolean operands.
Independent XML/JSON negation cases cover exactly one Boolean operand and reject missing/excess operands and nonboolean values.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures exercise binary arity for Eq/Ne/Gt/Ge/Lt/Le/In/Has, with numeric, membership and flags-enum compatibility cases.
Independent XML/JSON cases test logical operand counts and nonboolean operand rejection, including And/Or exact binary arity.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures exercise one through four operands in scalar and direct collection contexts, reject nonboolean conditions and incompatible branches, and accept two operands only in collections.

Independent XML qualified-member expressions and JSON enum-member strings cover valid members, flags-only combinations, missing members, wrong enum types, missing XML qualification and mixed-type XML combinations.
Independent XML/JSON cases cover variable and floating scale, large numeric values, exponent and special-value applicability, and malformed numeric forms.

Independent XML/JSON cases cover empty and Unicode strings, named/numeric XML references and JSON escaping. XML attribute and element notation share the constant cases. Invalid literal/escaped XML attribute characters fail in both strict and tolerant profiles; JSON nonstring values are rejected.
Independent XML/JSON cases cover empty, padded and unpadded base64url values, legal alphabet, terminal unused bits, padding counts, and malformed lengths/characters.
Independent XML/JSON cases cover true/false and reject nonboolean spellings, strings and numeric values.
Independent XML/JSON cases cover Int64 endpoints, overflow on both sides, fractional values and nonnumeric text.

Independent XML/JSON cases cover finite fractions/exponents, INF/-INF/NaN and invalid spellings. XML rejects noncanonical nonfinite spellings before normalization; JSON numeric expressions remain compatible with floating terms.
Independent XML/JSON timestamp constants cover required timezone, offset limits, calendar validity, leap seconds, omitted seconds, fractional precision and end-of-day rejection.
Independent XML/JSON time constants cover clock boundaries, leap/omitted seconds, fractions and malformed widths/fractions, rejecting timezone suffixes.

Independent XML/JSON duration constants cover negative and fractional day-time values and reject year/month/week units, empty durations, missing time components and duplicated/out-of-order components.

Independent XML expressions and term-typed JSON strings cover valid leap dates, century leap rules, invalid day/month bounds, lexical widths and forbidden time-zone suffixes; annotation diagnostics participate in validity.
Independent XML/JSON constants accept both hex cases and nil UUIDs, and reject nonhex characters, incorrect lengths, missing separators and braces.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover qualified set/singleton endpoints, containment rooted at in-scope singletons, forbidden set-root traversal, missing/out-of-scope roots, complex/containment traversal and collection-valued intermediate segment rejection.

Static duplicate-path rejection and distinct cast paths have independent paired-format evidence. The paragraph also describes runtime entity membership and most-specific binding selection; decomposed explicitly in conformance-obligations.json.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover required targets identifying sets, singletons and containment navigation, via simple names or target paths, with missing/invalid target negatives. Detailed traversal and runtime binding selection remain separately tracked.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures accept local sets/singletons, reject a name available only in another container, and accept its qualified cross-container path.
Independent XML and JSON source cases cover required Path/Target, object/string JSON shapes, and strict JSON rejection of qualified same-container targets.

Independent XML and JSON cases for set/singleton sources cover direct, complex, derived entity/complex and repeated containment paths. Negative cases isolate absent required casts, unrelated casts, missing/structural endpoints, terminal containment and intermediate non-containment navigation.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures exercise import identifiers and duplicate names across action/function imports, sets and singletons, with valid distinct-name controls.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover absent and authored boolean nullability in 4.0/4.01. JSON cases additionally assert effective default false and reject null, numeric and string values.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures for actions/functions with scalar and collection entity returns accept local set names and cross-container target paths, and reject missing sets/containers and singleton endpoints.

Independent source fixtures cover required import names and operation references, including absent and null JSON references. Optional entity-set targets have paired-format cases; service-document behavior is tracked separately.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures reject bound-only, missing and wrong-kind function references and directly assert all unbound overloads are exposed while bound overloads are excluded.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures accept unbound action imports and reject bound, unresolved and wrong-kind operation references. Function references have parallel cases, but their all-overloads obligation remains separate.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover required declaration names and type members, including missing or invalid types. JSON entity sets use Collection=true; omission denotes a singleton. Optional attribute semantics are tracked separately.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover subtype narrowing, same/unrelated type rejection, forbidden member-kind changes and action/function import redeclarations through an intermediate base container.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures reject invalid/empty identifiers and duplicate names across entity sets, singletons and action/function imports, with distinct-name positive controls.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures accept entity targets and reject complex, primitive, unresolved and absent/invalid types for entity sets and singletons.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures assert resolved scalar/collection multiplicity for actions and functions. JSON rejects nonboolean collection markers and XML-style Collection(...) type strings for parameters and returns.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover primitive, entity, complex, enum and type-definition parameters as scalars and collections on actions/functions, reject unknown namespace and primitive types, and distinguish required XML types from JSON defaults.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover matching and differing return types within bound/unbound overload groups, separate binding groups, and both directions of scalar/collection mismatch.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover required names, required XML types, invalid JSON type values, and the permitted omitted JSON type default on actions and functions. Optional facet semantics remain tracked separately.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures for actions and functions prove binding-parameter roots, navigation and derived casts, and rejection of other parameter roots, structural properties, missing members, unrelated casts and empty segments.
Independent XML and JSON source fixtures require XML operation names and JSON action/function kinds, with positive coverage of optional binding and entity-set-path declarations.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover optional action returns, required function returns, scalar and collection primitive/entity/complex types, and unresolved namespace or primitive types.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures for actions and functions accept absent Nullable and reject either authored boolean on entity-collection returns.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures distinguish bound target types and collection multiplicity, reject duplicate binding types despite different remaining parameters, and reject unbound overloads.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover valid, duplicate, empty, and invalid parameter identifiers on bound and unbound actions and functions.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures for bound and unbound functions isolate unordered parameter-name collisions (including reversed order), ordered type collisions with distinct names, and valid distinct signatures.
Independent source cases accept both constraint attributes and reject either or both missing; JSON equivalents also exercise invalid principal values and empty dependent paths.

Independent XML and JSON fixtures prove direct and recursive complex-property paths for entity and complex owners, owner-relative resolution, malformed/missing paths, forbidden intermediate navigation traversal, and endpoint type compatibility.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures cover all four actions and reject absent XML Action, null JSON action, and unknown action names.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures reject terminal containment and accept traversal through containment to a non-containment binding endpoint.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures accept one containment parent and reject two, both on one type and across base/derived declarations.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures exercise both versions, scalar and collection properties, and complex types with and without containment.
Independent XML and JSON fixtures exercise recursive and non-recursive containment with nullable, required, and collection-valued partners. Collection partners have no Nullable facet.
Independent XML and JSON cases prove partner path origins, terminal navigation members, complex and derived traversal, forbidden navigation traversal, and reverse target compatibility.
Independent XML and JSON cases cover matching and mismatching scalar types and the complex-type exception for entity and complex owners.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover member identifiers, combined member uniqueness, inherited kind collisions and proper subtype narrowing for entity/complex owners in 4.0 versus 4.01.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures prove combined structural/navigation member uniqueness and declaring-type name prohibition, including permitted inherited/base-name cases and prohibited narrowing redeclarations.
Independent source fixtures cover required members, every enum integer boundary, flags, implicit XML value order, primitive-only definitions and re-specification prohibition for each inherited facet.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures prove entity target kinds/scope, collection Nullable prohibition, complex-owner Partner prohibition, partner reciprocity and all referential nullability combinations.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover decimal versus temporal precision bounds, scale/precision ordering and case-insensitive floating scale version guards. Variable scale casing is accepted and output normalized to lowercase.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures cover declared/inherited keys for sets and containment collections, complete related keys including navigation on complex values, and alias identifier/uniqueness rules across inherited structural/navigation properties.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures exercise key scalar types, nullability, collection rejection, enum/type-definition keys, nested complex paths and direct-property alias prohibition. Related-entity and inherited alias obligations have separate focused evidence.
Independent XML/JSON fixtures prove inheritance cycle checks, open/media/abstract inheritance restrictions and version-specific declared/inherited key requirements.

Independent source fixtures cover schema type-name uniqueness, reserved namespaces, alias identifiers and XML schema/external annotation-group required members. Mixed global-namespace and cross-document obligations remain partial.
Independent XML and JSON positive/negative source fixtures cover required reference/include members, array/object shape, filters and document-global included namespace uniqueness.
Normative wording occurs inside an illustrative vocabulary annotation, not a CSDL authoring rule.
Explicit IEEE754Compatible and metadata options, arbitrary precision decimals and loader-backed graph validation are implemented. Exhaustive clause evidence remains open.
Default/control-field omission is a size optimization, not a reason to reject a semantically valid model.
Strict source parsing rejects namespace-qualified references where an alias exists and qualified same-container binding targets; tolerant parsing accepts them.
Case-only names, unknown future AppliesTo values, explicit 4.0 collection nullability, queryability and binding coverage do not make strict validity fail; no dedicated warning stream yet.
Obligation concerns runtime entity values, URLs, payloads, or execution rather than static metadata.
Reference annotations and Core.SchemaVersion inspection hooks are implemented. Retrieval query policy belongs to the caller; exhaustive clause evidence remains partial.

Independent XML/JSON fixtures prove ordered integer indexes, retained signed index values, item-relative traversal and resulting multiplicity. Runtime index evaluation is outside static scope; the mixed paragraph remains partial with reviewed atomic obligations.
Strict grammar regression tests cover missing/multiple document wrappers and required version/schema structure.
Document-global alias collision/reserved-name tests run before normalization.
Absent authored defaults and length facets stay absent; consumer code must not invent a service constraint.
